question: When the exact training examples and optimizer budget are fixed, how does allocating updates between phrase completion and sentence completion change each measured behavior?
hypothesis: Increasing phrase-completion updates from 1 to 16 to 32 will increase phrase completion performance and may trade off sentence completion. The 1:63 treatment may preserve the strong sentence effect seen in F023 while remaining weak on phrase questions. No monotonicity or aggregate-win claim is assumed.

design.single_changed_factor: task exposure allocation across a fixed 64-example support cohort
design.paired_seed_rule: For a given seed and task, all exposure treatments consume prefixes from the same independently seeded per-task example stream; cohort, model revision, LoRA initialization seed, optimizer, update budget and hyperparameters remain fixed.

training.device: cpu (MPS unavailable in this process at registration)

evaluation.prior_inspection: All F025 development questions were already inspected in F021-F023. This is exploratory mechanism study only; these data cannot establish independent generalization or promote a candidate.
primary_outcomes: trusted-key exact completion accuracy, reported separately for phrase and sentence tasks
sentence accuracy separately for singular and plural subjects
paired family-level bootstrap contrasts among the three exposure conditions
controls: unedited base arm, recorded in each paired evaluation campaign
task-matched prompt-only arm, recorded in each paired evaluation campaign
per-treatment, per-seed layerwise effective-delta-norm-matched random adapter, using the same evaluation questions
no aggregate-only score will hide phrase/sentence tradeoffs
evaluation.planned_arm_question_pairs: 6 trained adapters x (base + prompt + adapter + random) x 428 questions
evaluation.independent_confirmation: None in F025. The v3 confirmation families were consumed and retired by F024. If a pattern is selected for confirmation, generate new lexical and grammatical families before evaluating a frozen treatment.

analysis_and_limits.resampling_unit: whole benchmark family, paired across arms
analysis_and_limits.uncertainty: 95% paired family bootstrap intervals; only 7 phrase-development families exist, so phrase estimates are highly uncertain and descriptive
analysis_and_limits.multiplicity: three conditions, two seeds, multiple task-specific outcomes; treat intervals as exploratory, not confirmatory
analysis_and_limits.causal_scope: The manipulated factor is the complete task-exposure schedule, including its deterministic order; this study does not isolate update count from optimization-order effects.
analysis_and_limits.promotion: Not eligible. No training, selection, or tuning on final confirmation data; no transfer claims to other models or Astra.

controls_for_data_effects.example_identity: The exact same 64 example IDs and trusted answers appear in every condition.
controls_for_data_effects.family_overlap: One example per family within each task; no dev or confirmation examples enter the cohort.
controls_for_data_effects.repetition: Sampling is with replacement to reach 64 updates. Per-task streams are seed-specific and nested across the exposure ratios; repeated example IDs are logged per update.
additional_measured_fields: per-update training example ID and task type
effective delta norms per adapted layer
raw model responses and trusted grades
